title: Deadlock
context: What is a deadlock, and how do you prevent it?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: A deadlock happens when threads wait for each other in a cycle. Thread A holds lock 1 and waits for lock 2, while thread B holds lock 2 and waits for lock 1. Four conditions are needed: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. To prevent it, break one: always acquire locks in one global order, use tryLock with a timeout, or avoid nested locks. Detect it with a thread dump (jstack) that shows the blocked threads and their lock owners.

points.title: Circular wait
points.why: Two threads take the same locks in opposite order, so each waits forever.

points.title: Lock ordering
points.why: Acquiring locks in a fixed global order removes the cycle.

points.title: Diagnose with a thread dump
points.why: jstack shows which thread holds and waits for each lock.
